key_insight: A symmetry- and thermodynamics-preserving neural density functional can learn ion correlations in polymer electrolytes and generalize across salt concentration, geometry, and length scale.
engineering_relevance: This enables more reliable multiscale prediction of ionic structure and response in polymer electrolyte materials, supporting better design of batteries and other ion-conducting devices.
method: Trained a neural density functional on planar density and internal-force profiles from molecular dynamics.
Built in spatial symmetries, thermodynamic integrability, and Noether identities to preserve physics.
Used the model to predict density profiles, bulk structure factors, and long-wavelength number response in unseen conditions and larger domains.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports accurate predictions at an untrained salt concentration and stronger transfer to larger domains and 2D external fields than three alternative neural DFT architectures, with robustness maintained using only a quarter of the training runs.
watch_item: Performance is reported from a specific ion dataset and geometry set, so transferability to chemically different electrolytes or highly non-bulk regimes still needs validation.
paper_title: A structure-preserving neural density functional for the ions of a polymer electrolyte
